L104: ## New! Canada Impact+ Research Training Awards
L105: 
L106: On December 9, 2025, Canada’s tri-agencies announced the Canada Impact+ Research Training Awards (CIRTA) — a groundbreaking initiative to support the next generation of researchers.
L107: 
L108: What is it?
L109: 
L110:   * 600 doctoral scholarships across Canada
L111:   * Valued at $40,000 per year for three years
L112:   * Available to international students or Canadian students currently studying abroad and returning to Canada
L113: The University of Waterloo is thrilled to leverage this opportunity to attract exceptional research talent to our community.
L114: 
L115: 【57†Learn more about the application processes and deadlines】.
L116: ## International students
L117: 
L118: International students in full-time research-based master’s programs may be awarded an 【58†International Master’s Award of Excellence (IMAE)】 by their Faculty on top of any minimum funding received.
L119: 
L120: International students in a full-time PhD program will be awarded an 【59†International Doctoral Student Award (IDSA)】 , which is approximately the difference between full-time domestic PhD tuition and full-time international PhD tuition.
L121: Explore additional 【60†funding opportunities for international students】.
L122: As an international student, you may be eligible for funding through one of the University of Waterloo’s international agreements and sponsorships, which are formal agreements that are preset with governments and institutions abroad. If you are applying for graduate studies under one of these formal agreements, please review 【61†Waterloo’s sponsorship requirements】 which are an important part of your application process.
L123: Please note that international agreements and sponsorships may replace the minimum funding and IDSA.
L124: ## Self-funded full-time doctoral studies
L125: 
L126: Pursuing self-funded, full-time doctoral studies is available only on an exceptional basis, and must be approved by the academic unit and faculty of intended doctoral studies.
L127: 
L128: The following conditions will apply:
L129:   * Evidence of sufficient external sponsorship and/or personal funds to cover all 【36†study and living costs】 for the duration of your program. Note: This could include providing official documentation such as a sponsorship letter from an institution or a person providing you with funding, or personal bank statements from the past six months.

L23:   * ...from students of all nationalities
L24:   * ...in any field

L27:   * ...from students of any age
L28: 
L29: Please note that you need to apply for the scholarship in your major field of study.
L30: ## 2. Who is not allowed to apply?
L31: 
L32: We would like to remind you again here that you cannot get a study placement at Freie Universität Berlin by applying for a Deutschlandstipendium. At the time of application, you must already have received your acceptance notification or already be enrolled in the first semester (or higher) of your degree program.
L33: 
L34: The following are not allowed to apply:
L35:   * Students who are not enrolled at Freie Universität Berlin
L36:   * Students who applied for a study placement at Freie Universität, but who did not receive a letter of acceptance
L37:   * Students who will have exceeded the standard time to degree in the funding year they want to apply for.
L38:   * Doctoral students at Freie Universität Berlin. Doctoral students can learn about other sources of funding at Freie Universität Berlin through the 【3†university’s graduate studies portal】.
L39:   * Students at Charité – Universitätsmedizin Berlin. They have their own Deutschlandstipendium program: Charité – Universitätsmedizin Berlin’s 【4†website†nachwuchs.charite.de】 with information on their Deutschlandstipendium program.
L40:   * Students who are concurrently enrolled at multiple institutions, but whose main university of enrollment is not Freie Universität Berlin (i.e. who are not paying their semester fees to Freie Universität Berlin)
